species_guide.title: Field Reference Catalogue
species_guide.subtitle: Diagnostic field marks, ecology, conservation status and International Sign description for every species the model recognises. Cards are sorted alphabetically following the AOS 2024 taxonomy.
species_guide.footer_title: How the model recognises these species
species_guide.footer_text: The image-classification pipeline uses transfer learning over ImageNet-pretrained CNNs, with ResNet-50 as the baseline model. It supports AMP, warmup + cosine scheduling, class weighting, Mixup and CutMix to mitigate imbalance between abundant species (Buteo jamaicensis, Cathartes aura) and rare ones (Harpia harpyja, Morphnus guianensis, Falco deiroleucus). Grad-CAM is used as the explainability protocol to audit which image region drives the decision.
species_guide.references: References: Howell & Webb (1995); Berlanga et al. (2019); Bildstein (2006); Liguori (2005, 2011); AOS Check-list (64th–65th Supp.); IUCN Red List (2025); NOM-059-SEMARNAT-2010.

data.export_intro: Download your observations for personal use, scientific analysis, or submission to iNaturalist, GBIF and global biodiversity platforms.
data.export_internal_desc: All your saved observations in the application's native format. Useful for personal logs and local analysis.
data.export_dwc_desc: Standardised biodiversity format following the TDWG Darwin Core schema. Ready to upload to iNaturalist, GBIF or any open-data publisher.
data.export_feedback_desc: Every correction submitted via the feedback button. Used as the input for the next model retraining cycle.
data.ala_howto_title: How to upload your observations to iNaturalist / GBIF
data.ala_howto_step1: Sign in (or create a free account) at www.inaturalist.org.
data.ala_howto_step2: Go to Observations → Import → Upload CSV.
data.ala_howto_step3: Upload the raptors_mx_observations_dwc.csv file you just downloaded.
data.ala_howto_step4: iNaturalist will validate the records and integrate them into the global biodiversity network (typical 24-72h for community review).
data.ala_howto_note: The identifiedBy column credits the AI explicitly so reviewers can apply appropriate weight to AI-assisted records.
